title: Fugue in D major
blurb: More entries than any other fugue in Book II: twenty-three of them in fifty bars.
card: Fifteen stretto pairs, more than any fugue here, and four entries stacked inside a bar at the end.
history: Nine notes, a bar and a bit, and nothing that reliably comes back with it. What Bach has instead is overlap: the analysis counts fifteen stretto pairs here, more than in any other fugue on the site. The entries thicken as the piece goes on, and the last four begin a crotchet apart, one voice after another, across bars 44 and 45.

It is written in cut time, which normally signals minims and crotchets moving broadly. This one moves in crotchets and quavers. Take the alla breve at face value and the entries a crotchet apart stop being separable by ear.

Book II was put together in Leipzig around 1739–42, nearly twenty years after Book I, out of pieces Bach had been writing over a much longer span. The main source is the London autograph in the British Library, some of it in his hand, some in Anna Magdalena's.
